deliverables: Ongoing maintenance, bug fixes, dependency upkeep, security patches, and releases for the existing Scalus stack and supported export targets
Initial Plutus V4 support in the compiler and standard library for a Dijkstra developer preview
Updates for Dijkstra-related ledger rules, transaction building, builtins, cost models, nested transactions, accounts, guard scripts, and conformance testing
Improved JS/TS interfaces and documentation for Scalus components embedded in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, and Lucid Evolution
Java/Kotlin integration examples for Spring Boot and Ktor and cleaner integration with Cardano Client Lib and Yaci
Foundational application runtime components including reactive workers, chain follower, and task scheduler
request.what: Fund a 9-month continuation of Scalus focused on maintenance, Dijkstra hard-fork readiness, interoperability, and a scoped application runtime.

claims.claim: Scalus is presented as an established open-source Cardano development platform built by Lantr Engineering over three years of continuous delivery.
The proposal states that Scalus is used directly by Gummiworm L2, Bifrost, SugarRush, Vela, and DID/DIDComm.
The proposal states that Scalus components are reused in MeshJS, Evolution SDK, Lucid Evolution, Cardano Client Lib, and YaciDevKit.
The proposal says Scalus has 4,642 commits across 32 releases, 12 contributors, and more than 20,000 monthly Scalus.js downloads.
The requested budget is ₳2,464,844 for 9 months, described as about $394,375 at a $0.16/ADA reference rate with no contingency.
The proposer states this resubmission reduced the prior proposal from ₳8.503M over 12 months to about ₳2.465M over 9 months and reduced FTE from 8.25 to 2.25.
The funded scope excludes a standalone L1 node, full Gummiworm L2 integration, broad formal verification, and advanced devnet expansion.

Delivery is described as three quarterly milestones from July 2026 through March 2027, with maintenance running continuously and Dijkstra readiness, interoperability, and runtime work phased across milestones.
The proposal states delivery will be milestone-based and administered through audited SundaeSwap treasury contracts with an independent oversight board and third-party assurance.

The proposer argues Scalus supports Cardano 2030 adoption and utility indirectly by improving developer infrastructure for teams building applications rather than by directly producing TVL, transactions, or users.

summary: The document requests ₳2,464,844 for Lantr Engineering to continue Scalus for 9 months, emphasizing maintenance, Dijkstra readiness, interoperability, and a scoped runtime, with several adoption and governance claims that are mostly asserted in the supplied text.
